key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset after trauma. LOCATION: BELOW level of injury. DURATION: Immediate onset, symptoms persist. CHARACTER: PARALYSIS, numbness, weakness. AGGRAVATING: MOVEMENT, pressure. RELIEVING: IMMEDIATE medical intervention, supportive care. TIMING: Immediate onset, symptoms persist. SEVERITY: 8-10/10, severe and unrelenting. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: PARALYSIS, numbness, weakness, may have bowel/bladder dysfunction, may have respiratory problems. KEY POSITIVES: Paralysis, numbness, weakness, bowel/bladder dysfunction. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe respiratory distress - possible respiratory failure, call 911
Signs of respiratory failure - difficulty breathing, cyanosis, altered mental status - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
Signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
